entry.title: France 24: Discussion on AI Safety and the Future of AI Development

link.title: France 24: Discussion on AI Safety and the Future of AI Development

entry.content:
I was featured on France 24 Español discussing critical topics in artificial intelligence development.

Topics Discussed

The segment covered several important themes in the current AI landscape:

AI Safety vs. Rapid Development

The tension between pushing AI capabilities forward and ensuring these systems are safe and aligned with human values.

Constitutional AI

How approaches like Anthropic’s Constitutional AI attempt to build safety directly into AI training, creating systems that are helpful, harmless, and honest.

Industry Dynamics

The competitive landscape between major AI companies like Anthropic and OpenAI, and how different philosophies on safety and development speed shape the industry.

Watch the Segment

It was an honor to contribute to this important public conversation about the future of AI and the responsibility we have in developing these powerful technologies.

Originally shared on LinkedIn
entry.summary: Featured on France 24 Español discussing AI safety, Constitutional AI, and industry tensions

entry.title: IFE Conference: The Future of AI in Education

link.title: IFE Conference: The Future of AI in Education

entry.content:
I presented research at the IFE Conference (Institute for the Future of Education) alongside Dr. Victor Rodriguez.

Research Focus

Our collaboration explored the future of AI in education, examining:

  • AI-powered personalized learning systems
  • Intelligent tutoring technologies
  • Assessment automation and feedback
  • Educational data mining and analytics
  • Ethical frameworks for AI in academia

Collaboration

It was a great pleasure to work with Dr. Victor Rodriguez on this research. The IFE Conference brings together educators, researchers, and technologists to discuss innovations that will shape the future of learning.

The intersection of artificial intelligence and education presents tremendous opportunities to improve learning outcomes while also raising important questions about equity, privacy, and the role of human educators.

entry.title: SLICE: Semantic Language-Indexed Code Extraction at NeurIPS 2025

link.title: SLICE: Semantic Language-Indexed Code Extraction at NeurIPS 2025

entry.content:
Our paper SLICE: Semantic Language-Indexed Code Extraction was presented at the LatinX in AI Workshop at NeurIPS 2025 in San Diego.

About SLICE

SLICE introduces a novel approach to code extraction that leverages semantic understanding of natural language queries to identify and extract relevant code segments. The system:

  • Indexes code using semantic representations
  • Matches natural language queries to code functionality
  • Extracts relevant code snippets with high precision
  • Supports multiple programming languages

Research Team

Congratulations to the team on this achievement:

  • Oscar Arámbula
  • Oscar Beltran
  • Omar Guzmán
  • Victor Terrón

Presenting at NeurIPS, one of the premier conferences in machine learning, and being part of the LatinX in AI community was an incredible honor.

Originally shared on LinkedIn
entry.summary: Presenting SLICE at the LatinX in AI Workshop at NeurIPS 2025 in San Diego

entry.title: MICAI 2025 Panel: Generative AI’s Impact on Education

  • Academic integrity in the age of AI assistants
  • Personalized learning through AI tutors
  • Assessment redesign for AI-enabled environments
  • Preparing students for an AI-augmented workforce
  • Ethical considerations in AI education tools

Distinguished Panelists

  • Omar Florez
  • Pablo Rivas
  • Inés Alvarez-Icaza
  • Xiaoou Li
  • Lourdes Martinez

entry.title: Beyond SWE-Bench: Multi-language Automated Program Repair at MICAI 2025

link.title: Beyond SWE-Bench: Multi-language Automated Program Repair at MICAI 2025

entry.content:
Our paper “Beyond SWE-Bench: A Compiler-Assisted Pipeline for Multi-language Automated Program Repair” was published at MICAI 2025.

Research Summary

This work extends beyond the popular SWE-Bench benchmark to address automated program repair across multiple programming languages. Our compiler-assisted pipeline leverages:

  • Static analysis for bug localization
  • Compiler feedback loops for repair validation
  • Multi-language support beyond Python-only benchmarks
  • Improved repair accuracy through structured reasoning

Team

This research was a collaborative effort with:

  • Moises Pineda
  • Diego Luna
  • Mariana Esquivel
  • Juan Salazar
  • Prof. Daniel Flores Araiza

The paper contributes to the growing field of AI-assisted software engineering by demonstrating how compiler integration can improve the reliability of automated repairs.

Originally shared on LinkedIn
entry.summary: Paper on compiler-assisted pipeline for automated program repair published at MICAI 2025

entry.title: CIMPS 2025: LLM Optimization Techniques for Compliance Assessment

link.title: CIMPS 2025: LLM Optimization Techniques for Compliance Assessment

entry.content:
PhD student Victor Terrón presented his research on LLM optimization techniques for compliance assessment at CIMPS 2025 in Lima, Peru.

Research Overview

The work provides a comprehensive analysis of 9 different optimization techniques for Large Language Models in the context of software compliance assessment:

Techniques Analyzed

  1. RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) - Enhancing LLM responses with retrieved context
  2. LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) - Efficient fine-tuning of large models
  3. Prompt Engineering - Optimizing input prompts for better outputs
  4. Fine-tuning strategies - Domain-specific model adaptation
  5. Chain-of-thought prompting - Structured reasoning approaches
  6. And more…

Key Findings

The research demonstrates how these techniques can be applied to improve the accuracy and reliability of LLMs when assessing software compliance with industry standards and regulations.

Congratulations to Victor on this excellent presentation!

Originally shared on LinkedIn
entry.summary: PhD student Victor Terrón presents research on optimizing LLMs for software compliance

entry.title: 80 Students Build Autonomous Coding Agents at Tec de Monterrey

link.title: 80 Students Build Autonomous Coding Agents at Tec de Monterrey

entry.content:
Last week marked the conclusion of one of the most ambitious capstone projects we’ve undertaken at Tecnológico de Monterrey. Over the course of a semester, 80 students built autonomous coding agents by fine-tuning small language models on specific code repositories.

The Challenge

Students were tasked with creating AI assistants capable of reasoning about code problems. This wasn’t just about using existing tools—they had to:

  • Apply compiler techniques to filter and curate datasets from large code corpora
  • Fine-tune language models on repository-specific codebases
  • Deploy cloud-based APIs for their AI assistants
  • Build agents with genuine reasoning capabilities

Technical Achievements

The teams demonstrated impressive technical sophistication:

  • Custom dataset curation pipelines
  • Model fine-tuning with LoRA and other efficient techniques
  • Cloud deployment on Modal infrastructure
  • Integration with real-world development workflows

Industry Partnership

This project wouldn’t have been possible without our partners:

  • C3 AI - Training and mentorship support
  • Modal Labs - Cloud infrastructure for deployment
  • Faculty support from Victor Rodriguez, Daniel Flores Araiza, Rodolfo Castelló, and Liliana Barbosa

Several teams were invited to present their findings in Redwood City, demonstrating the industry relevance of their work.

Why This Matters

Technology education must stay current with industry demands. Academic programs should bridge the gap between classical computer science fundamentals and emerging agentic AI applications. This capstone shows that students can master cutting-edge AI techniques while building practical, deployable solutions.

The future of software development is increasingly AI-augmented, and our graduates are ready to lead that transformation.
entry.summary: A semester-long capstone project where students fine-tuned language models to create AI coding assistants

entry.title: AI-Powered Quality Assurance - A 10-Week Capstone Journey

link.title: AI-Powered Quality Assurance - A 10-Week Capstone Journey

entry.content:
This semester marked the conclusion of an intensive 10-week capstone project at Tecnológico de Monterrey’s Campus Guadalajara. I had the privilege of coaching 15 projects for graduating Computer Science students, all focused on a fascinating challenge: using AI to analyze visual elements in software testing.

Beyond Code Analysis

Traditional testing tools focus on code. Our students explored a different approach—how can AI effectively identify visual discrepancies, design issues, and other subtle errors that humans typically catch during manual testing?

Student Solutions

The teams developed diverse and innovative solutions:

  • Accessibility testing prototypes - AI-powered tools to detect accessibility issues in user interfaces
  • Visual defect detection systems - Automated identification of UI inconsistencies
  • Natural language automation frameworks - Test case generation from plain English descriptions
  • SEO optimization tools - AI-driven analysis of web content for search engine visibility

Key Learnings

What made this cohort special was their willingness to experiment. They quickly learned that:

  1. Visual AI requires different training approaches than code analysis
  2. Edge cases in UI testing are vast and varied
  3. Human-AI collaboration is essential for QA workflows

Acknowledgments

Special thanks to:

  • C3 AI - Our training partner throughout the program
  • Carlos Ovidio Quirarte Arnauda and Cesar Mancillas for industry guidance
  • Luis Guillermo Hernández-Rojas and professors Liliana and Víctor Rodriguez for institutional support

Watching these students grow from uncertain beginners to confident AI practitioners has been incredibly rewarding. Their dedication to solving real-world problems with innovative AI solutions gives me great hope for the future of software engineering.
entry.summary: Mentoring 15 teams of graduating CS students to build AI tools for visual software testing

entry.title: Exploring Catalonia’s AI Ecosystem - A fAIrLAC Jalisco Mission

link.title: Exploring Catalonia’s AI Ecosystem - A fAIrLAC Jalisco Mission

entry.content:
As part of the fAIrLAC Jalisco program, a delegation from Tecnológico de Monterrey’s AI Hub visited Catalonia to explore their thriving artificial intelligence ecosystem. The week-long mission provided invaluable insights into how a region can strategically develop AI capabilities.

Catalonia.IA Strategy

We had the opportunity to learn about Catalonia.IA, the regional government’s comprehensive AI strategy. The approach integrates:

  • Research excellence at universities
  • Hospital and healthcare partnerships
  • Industry collaboration frameworks
  • Ethical AI guidelines

Key Visits

Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya (UPC)

Met with researchers Raul Benitez Iglesias and Christian Mata, who focus on health and AI applications. Their work on diabetic retinopathy detection and cardiotoxicity assessment showcased the potential of AI in clinical settings.

Healthcare Innovation

  • Hospital de la Santa Creu i Sant Pau
  • Barcelona Children’s Hospital
  • Xartec Salut health technology cluster

Research Centers

  • CIDAI - Catalonia’s AI research center
  • CataloniaBio - Life sciences cluster

Topics Explored

Our discussions covered critical themes for responsible AI development:

  • Healthtech applications - From diagnosis to treatment optimization
  • Ethics in AI - Building frameworks for the LAC region
  • Women in AI - Initiatives to increase female participation
  • AI democratization - Making AI accessible to non-technical audiences

Building Bridges

Special thanks to:

  • The Catalonia Government Delegation in Mexico and Central America for facilitating this knowledge exchange
  • Colleagues Gilberto Ochoa-Ruiz, Juan Roberto Hernández Villalobos, and Gerardo Rodriguez Hernandez
  • Prof. Karina Gibert (IDEAI-UPC) for discussions on gender equity in AI

This visit reinforced that international collaboration is essential for developing AI that benefits society. The partnerships initiated here will continue to grow as we work together on socially-responsible AI initiatives.
entry.summary: A week-long exploration of Catalonia's artificial intelligence strategy and collaboration opportunities
